stem: Navya looks at a grey fuzzy patch of mould on a slice of old bread. With her unaided eyes she cannot see separate tiny living organisms. Her teacher says microorganisms may still be present.

parts.text: Which claim correctly says how Navya should observe those tiny organisms?

options.text: She needs a magnifying glass or microscope because the organisms are too small for the unaided eye.
An ordinary magnifying glass is enough to see the tiniest microorganisms clearly.
A microscope is required to see the whole slice of bread.
A flat windowpane can be used as a magnifying glass to see them.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Objects below a certain size cannot be seen with the unaided eye; curved glass or a microscope makes them appear larger so they can be observed.

teacher.key_rationale: Tiny organisms on the mould are below unaided-eye size, so a magnifying glass or microscope is needed. An ordinary magnifying glass may not show the tiniest ones clearly; a whole bread slice does not need a microscope; a flat windowpane does not magnify.
